---
title: "Repair and review (PIP-FUCCI)"
---

On PIP-FUCCI plates, tracks can be repaired automatically and then checked
by a reviewer in napari, with an agent's help if you like. Nothing edits the tracker's output. Corrections are entries in an
**edit log**, and the curated lineage is always rebuilt from the automatic
repair plus that log, so it can be reproduced, inspected and undone.

::: {.callout-important}
## Naming PIP-FUCCI channels

A plate is treated as PIP-FUCCI only if it is a timelapse and has one channel
named exactly `pip` and one named exactly `geminin` (any case; a `_nucleus` or
`_cell` role suffix is allowed). Any other name, such as `Geminin_488`, `Cdt1`
or `pip_mCherry`, means the plate is not FUCCI. Its tracks are then not
repaired, and the review tools refuse it. Name the channels in the plate's
metadata before running the pipeline.
:::

## 1. Automatic repair

Cellpose often splits one nucleus into pieces, and the tracker then reports
divisions that never happened. The repair accepts a division only when both
daughters lose geminin, which is degraded at anaphase. It merges touching pieces
back, detaches mislinked neighbours and rejoins tracks that restart.

```bash
uv run cellview repair-tracks 5054 --dry-run     # report only
uv run cellview repair-tracks 5054               # write track_id / parent_track_id
```

The repair reads `track_id_raw` / `parent_track_id_raw` and writes `track_id` /
`parent_track_id`, so running it again gives the same result. `--well`
restricts it to some wells, and `--events FILE` writes every repair decision
to a CSV.

## 2. Review queue

Cells present at a start frame are followed to a stop frame. A random sample is
drawn per well. The cells the walker flags (lost, gaps, fragments, phases out of
order, rare outcomes) are queued, plus an audit fraction of the unflagged ones:

```bash
uv run cellview review-queue 5054 --well C2 --well C3 --sample 50 \
    --start 72 --stop 168 --audit 0.2 --seed 1 --out review/
```

This writes `review/queue.json` and `review/sample.csv`. Pass `--log
review/edits.jsonl` to build a queue on top of corrections already made.

## 3. Filmstrips

A filmstrip crops a window that follows the cell through every frame, with its
PIP, geminin and area traces underneath:

```bash
uv run omero-screen-images --env production track 5054 C2-t72-L524
uv run omero-screen-images --env production track 5054 \
    --queue review/queue.json --log review/edits.jsonl
```

## 4. Track Review widget

Open **Plugins → Track Review Widget** and load `review/queue.json`. For each
cell you can:

- link it to its continuation (click it, or press 1…9 for a numbered
  candidate);
- unlink it, or add or remove a nucleus;
- split a nucleus, or draw one that was missed;
- mark mitosis, death or slippage, or exclude the cell;
- give a verdict.

*Next break* jumps along the track to the next problem and *Follow cell* keeps
the cell in view, panning only when it leaves the central part of the view.
Edits go to `review/edits.jsonl` and verdicts to `review/decisions.json`.

Fluorescence channels open with their background black: contrast is set from
several timepoints, so a reporter that rises later in the movie (geminin in
S/G2) is not saturated. Brightfield channels (`bf`, `brightfield`, `phase`,
`dic`) are grey, sit underneath the fluorescence and start hidden; tick their
eye to show them.

### Track view

**Track view** (in the widget, beside *Filmstrip*) docks a lineage overview of
the well, in the manner of Mastodon's TrackScheme: one column per curated
track, time running down in hours, daughters forking from their mother at the
division, one node per frame with a mask and a dashed edge across frames
without one.

A track counts as divided only if the reviewer's outcome, a curated mitosis
or the fate walker says so (for a track the walker did not follow: at least
two tracker daughters of six frames or more). Other tracker parent links,
mostly short fragments, are drawn as faint dotted *splits* and are not used
for division alignment.

**Wells.** The well box lists every tracked well of the plate. Each well is
read from its own review directory, found among the siblings of the open
queue's directory (a directory with `edits.jsonl` and `correction.json` or
`queue.json` for that plate and well; the one reviewed most recently wins,
and the *review* box picks another or *CellView only*). Only the Track Review
session's own wells are interactive. In any other well a click moves the
viewer to the cell if that well's images are loaded, and otherwise only
describes it; it never opens the cell, whose edits belong to another log.

- **Colour** by phase, the track's verdict or outcome, frame flags (reviewer
  mask, a link or swap a reviewer confirmed, another edit, first frame after
  a gap) or edit density (edits per hour of track).
- **Align** on the absolute frame, the window start, the division, mitotic
  exit, G2 entry or S entry. Each lineage tree is shifted as a whole; trees
  without the event are hidden or, with *Unaligned* on, parked on the right.
- **Sort** by track id, length, outcome, event time or edit density.
- **Filter** by verdict (*accepted* = accept or correct), outcome, who
  reviewed the cell (agent, human, both), audited or flagged cells only, and
  a minimum length. A kept cell brings its daughters if they are long enough.

Mouse: wheel zooms, drag pans, right-drag zooms the axes separately. Zoomed
out, each track is a line in the mode's colours; zoomed in, nodes become
markers and then tracks get labels (review id, length, outcome, verdict,
reviewer, audit). Hovering a node shows its frame, label, area, PIP, geminin
and phase; **clicking it opens that cell in the Track Review widget at that
frame** (the queue item if the cell is queued, otherwise an ad-hoc item). The
cell open in the widget is highlighted in the view, and the view rebuilds
whenever `edits.jsonl` or a `*decisions.json` changes.

Phases start as the fate walker's per-frame G1/S/G2 calls and are replaced by
the HMM's G1/S/G2/E/X calls once those are computed in a background process
(about ten seconds per well). As in the fate build, the HMM uses a phase
reference fitted once on every tracked well of the plate (cached in
`~/.cache/omero-screen/track_view/`) and is called on the analysis window;
outside it, and on tracks shorter than six frames, the walker's call stays.

## Working with an agent

With [napari-mcp](https://github.com/HocheggerLab/napari-mcp/tree/plugin-tools)
installed, omero-screen-napari adds review tools to the agent through
napari-mcp's plugin hook. The agent can go to a cell, show its filmstrip, rank
candidate continuations and propose an edit. A proposal appears in the widget
and is applied only when the reviewer confirms it.

```bash
uv run --with "napari-mcp @ git+https://github.com/HocheggerLab/napari-mcp@plugin-tools" napari
claude mcp add --transport http napari http://127.0.0.1:9999/mcp
```

The plugin hook is on the `plugin-tools` branch of the HocheggerLab fork until
upstream napari-mcp releases it.

## The edit log on the command line

```bash
uv run cellview curate show review/edits.jsonl
uv run cellview curate add review/edits.jsonl link \
    --plate 5054 --well C2 --cell 72:524 --frame 156 --label 3132
uv run cellview curate undo review/edits.jsonl --plate 5054 --well C2
uv run cellview curate replay review/edits.jsonl --plate 5054 --write
```

`add` validates an edit against the plate before appending it. `undo` appends a
revert entry instead of deleting anything. `replay` rebuilds the curated lineage
from the automatic repair plus every live edit; `--write` stores it in CellView.
Every edit type and option is in the
[CellView CLI reference](../cellview/reference/cli/index.html).
